text.p: Newport Petroleum Corp and Cimarron Petroleum Ltd said on Thursday they agreed to merge under a share swap deal which will offer Cimarron shareholders Newport stock worth C$25.56 per share.

The stock swap will be subject to a minimum of 2.4 Newport shares for one Cimarron share and a maximum of 2.7 Newport shares. The market value of Newport shares will be based upon the weighted average trading price on the Toronto Stock Exchange during the ten trading days ending on the third business day before the offer expires.

Based on Newport's C$9.80 a share closing price on Wednesday, Cimarron shareholders would be entitled to 2.61 Newport shares for each of their Cimarron shares. Under this formula, a total of 37.62 million shares would be issued.
The merger is subject to the receipt of all appropriate regulatory approvals and a minimum of 66-2/3 percent of the outstanding shares being deposited under the offer.
The companies said the resulting entity, which will be called Newport Petroleum, will have a market capitalization in excess of C$750 million.

The reserve base of the merged company will include 380 billion cubic feet of natural gas and 20.3 million barrels of crude oil and natural gas liquids. The companies said that if the merger is completed, the combined company plans a C$125 million capital expenditure program in 1997.
The Cimarron board unanimously recommended that shareholders tender to the Newport offer. Cimarron board members intend to deposit their shares under the offer, the companies said.
Cimarron has agreed to pay a non-completion fee of C$11 million if it enters into a different takeover deal.
The companies said before this offer closes, Cimarron will redeem the rights issued under its shareholder rights protection plan or waive the application of the plan with respect to the merger.
